transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I came in because I keep getting this thought, like even after I do the safety check on my cab, my brain keeps saying I missed something. Like maybe something’s wrong and someone could get hurt, or my boss will think I lied about checking it. I know I checked, but it just keeps hitting me while I’m driving.

And I’m trying to study too, like I’m supposed to be focusing, but then it’s the same thing in my head, over and over. It’s kind of stupid because I know I did it, but I can’t make it shut up.
Do these thoughts about missing something in your safety check feel like they are coming into your mind against your will?

Yeah… it does feel like that. Like I’m not trying to think about it, I already did the check, but then it just pops back in like, “What if you missed something?” And then I’m driving and I should be watching the road, or later I’m trying to study, and it’s still there.

It’s annoying because I know I checked the cab, but my brain keeps going, like somebody could get hurt or my boss could say I lied about doing it. It’s not like I want to sit there thinking about that. It just keeps coming in.
Do these thoughts about missing something in your safety check cause you a lot of distress or anxiety?

Yeah, it does. Like, a lot. I’ll be driving and I know I checked the cab, but then it hits me again—what if I missed something and somebody gets hurt, or what if my boss thinks I lied about doing it?

And then I’m trying to focus on the road, or later I’m supposed to study, but it’s just… there. It’s like when you’ve got a song stuck in your head, except it’s not a song, it’s this stressful thing that makes my chest feel tight and I can’t relax. I’ll tell myself, “You already checked,” but it doesn’t really shut up.
Are you finding it harder to do your job or study because of these thoughts, or are they just making you feel anxious?

It’s… yeah, it’s more than just anxiety, I think. Like it actually messes up my day. I’ve lost rides because I can’t get out on the road on time, and I’ve gotten warnings for it too, which makes it worse because then I’m thinking about my boss watching me.

And with studying for my CDL, I keep saying I’m gonna sit down and do it, but then so much time is gone from checking or being stuck thinking about it that I push it back again. I used to hang out with friends more, but lately I barely see them because I’m either behind on work or trying to catch up on the studying I didn’t do. It’s like the whole day gets eaten up.
Have you been doing anything repeatedly, like checking the cab multiple times, to try and get rid of these thoughts?

Yeah… I mean, that’s kind of the whole problem. Before I take a ride, I’ll go around the car checking stuff, like the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, the paperwork… and then I’ll do it again. Sometimes I take pictures too, like proof that I checked it.

But then if one part doesn’t feel right, I’ll start the whole thing over. Like I’ll be almost done and then I’m thinking, “Wait, did I really check that back door?” and then I’m back at the beginning. It’s stupid because there’ll be a passenger waiting, or I’m already late, and I know they’re probably annoyed, but I still feel like I can’t just leave yet.

And then sometimes I start thinking about how my uncle used to always say if you’re gonna drive people around, you gotta be serious about the car, and I get that, but this is different. Like I’m not just being careful. I get stuck there.
Do you feel like you have to repeat these checks to make the thoughts about missing something go away?

Yeah… I do. It’s like I can’t move on until I do it again, even if I already checked.

I’ll go around the car—tires, lights, doors, the meter, the paperwork—and I’ll be like, okay, that should be enough. But then if it doesn’t feel right, I start thinking maybe I missed the back door or maybe the light didn’t actually work, and then I have to go back around. Sometimes I’ll take pictures too, like that should prove it to me, but then even that doesn’t always settle it.

And it’s dumb because there’ll be someone waiting, and I’m already late, and I’ll be thinking about how my uncle used to always be on me about doing things the right way with cars, like checking everything before driving, but this isn’t just that. I’m not just being responsible. I feel like I have to keep repeating it or I can’t leave.
Do you feel like if you don't repeat these checks, something bad will happen?

Yeah… kind of. Like, if I don’t do it, I get this feeling that I missed something important and then it’s gonna turn into a problem once I’m out driving.

So I’ll keep going around the car before I take a ride—tires, lights, doors, meter, paperwork—and even if I did it already, I’ll think, wait, did I really check it? Sometimes I take pictures, which sounds weird, but it’s like I need proof. And if one thing doesn’t feel right, I start the whole check over again.

It’s annoying because passengers can be standing there waiting, and I’m already late, and I still can’t just get in and go.
Do you think something specific and terrible would happen if you didn't repeat these checks?

Yeah… I mean, not like one exact scene every time, but it turns into that. Like I’ll think I missed something on the cab, and then somebody could get hurt because of it. Or my boss is gonna say I lied and didn’t really check it.

And it sticks in my head even when I know I did the safety check. Like I’ll be driving and still thinking, “What if I missed it?” It’s hard to shut it off. Even when I’m trying to study, it comes back, and then I’m thinking about the cab again instead of what I’m supposed to be doing.
Do you think that by repeating these checks, you are preventing something bad from happening?

Yeah… that’s what it feels like. Like if I do it enough times, then maybe I’m stopping something from going wrong.

Before I take a ride, I keep going around the car—tires, lights, doors, the meter, the paperwork—and I’ll tell myself, okay, this is the last time. But then it doesn’t feel right, or I think maybe I looked too fast, and I restart the whole thing. Sometimes I take pictures too, like that’ll make me believe it’s done, but then I still end up checking again.

And it’s embarrassing because people are standing there waiting, and I’m already late, and I’m thinking about all this instead of just driving. I know it probably looks ridiculous, but in my head it feels like I’m preventing a mistake or something bad by doing it again.
Do you feel like you have to do the checks a specific number of times or in a specific order to feel right?

Yeah… not like I have a magic number, exactly. It’s more the order and whether it feels finished. I usually go around the cab checking the tires, then lights, doors, the meter, paperwork… and if I get this feeling like I rushed it or maybe didn’t really look, I’ll start over.

Sometimes I’ll take pictures too, like proof for myself, but then I’ll still think, “Wait, was that enough?” It’s stupid because people are waiting, and I’m already late, and then I’m thinking about how they’re looking at me, and that makes me mess up the order more. So then I check again.
Do you feel like there's a specific way you have to do these checks, like a certain order or pattern, for them to feel complete?

Yeah, it’s like… I have to do it in that same sort of loop around the cab. Tires, lights, doors, meter, paperwork. And if I get to the end and it doesn’t feel complete, I can’t just leave it.

I’ll think, “No, you didn’t really check that,” and then I start the whole thing again. Sometimes I take pictures, like that should settle it, but then I’m standing there looking at the picture and still thinking maybe I missed something. And then passengers are waiting, and I’m already late, which makes me more nervous, so I mess myself up and do it again.
Do you feel like you're trying to get everything exactly right when you're doing these checks, or is it more about avoiding something bad from happening?

It’s… kind of both, I guess. Like I want it to be exactly right, but mostly because if it’s not right, then I start thinking something bad could happen or I missed something.

Before I take a ride, I keep going around the car—tires, lights, doors, the meter, the paperwork—and if one part feels off, I can’t just move on. I restart it. Sometimes I even take pictures, like that’ll prove I checked, but then I’m still standing there thinking, “Did I really look?” Meanwhile the passenger’s waiting, and I’m late, and then I get more stressed and do the whole thing again.

It’s annoying because other drivers just get in and go, you know? Like my uncle used to tell me, “Don’t waste time, time is money,” and I know that, I really do. But when I’m there by the cab, it feels like I have to get it right before I can leave.
Is it more important for you to do the checks perfectly or to just make sure nothing bad happens?

Mostly it’s making sure nothing bad happens, I think… but I get stuck on doing it perfectly because that’s the only way it feels safe.

Like before I take a ride, I keep going around the car—tires, lights, doors, meter, paperwork—and if something doesn’t feel right, I start over. Sometimes I take pictures too, like proof, but then I still don’t trust it. And it’s embarrassing because passengers are waiting, and I’m already late, and I know I look ridiculous just walking around the cab again and again.

My uncle used to say if you waste time you lose money, and I hear that in my head too, but I still can’t just get in and drive unless the check feels done.
Do you feel like you need to perform these checks in a way that feels symmetrical or balanced to you?

Not really symmetrical, like… not like both sides have to match or anything. It’s more that I have to do the whole round the right way.

Before I take a ride, I keep circling the cab checking the tires, lights, doors, the meter, the paperwork—sometimes I take pictures too, which sounds stupid when I say it. But if it doesn’t feel right, I restart the whole check. Even if someone’s already waiting in the back or I’m late, I still get stuck doing it again.
Do you feel like you're doing these checks to control something or to prevent something from happening?

Yeah… more to prevent something, I think. Like, if I don’t check it right, then I feel like something could go wrong once I start the ride.

So before I can take someone, I keep going around the car—tires, lights, doors, the meter, the paperwork—and I’ll do it again and again. Sometimes I take pictures, which is weird because then I’ll look at the picture and still think, “Wait, did I actually check?” And then I start the whole thing over if it doesn’t feel right.

It’s not like I’m trying to control everything in the world, I guess… though my uncle used to say you have to be in control of your car, especially driving people around. But yeah, mostly it’s like I’m trying to stop something bad from happening, even when the passenger is sitting there waiting and I’m already late.
Do you think that if you didn't repeat these checks, the bad things you worry about would definitely happen?

Not definitely, I guess… I know that sounds weird. Like, part of me knows just because I don’t check again doesn’t mean the tire will fall off or someone will get hurt. But the thought keeps hitting me that I missed something on the cab, even when I already did the safety check.

And then I start thinking, what if somebody gets hurt, or what if my boss says I lied about checking it? I’ll be driving or trying to study later and it’s still in my head, like I can’t make it shut up.

Sorry, I’m kind of going off… but no, I don’t think it’s definitely going to happen. It just feels like I can’t risk it.
Is the feeling that you need to repeat these checks more about fearing that you've made a mistake or fearing what might happen as a result of that mistake?

It’s kind of both, but… I think it starts with the mistake. Like, even when I know I did the safety check, this thought just hits me that I missed something on the cab.

And then right after that it turns into, “What if somebody gets hurt?” or “What if my boss says I lied about checking it?” I hate that one because I’m not trying to lie, you know? I’m just trying to do the job right.

And it doesn’t really stop after I leave, either. I’ll be driving or later trying to study, and it’s still in my head, like I can’t make it shut up.
Is your need to repeat these checks driven more by the desire to do everything perfectly or the fear of what might happen if you don't?

It’s more the fear of what happens if I don’t, I think. Like, I want it done right, obviously, but before I take a ride I’ll keep walking around the cab checking the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, the paperwork… then I’ll do it again.

Sometimes I even take pictures, and then I’m looking at the picture thinking, wait, did I really check that or did I just take the picture? And then I start over because it doesn’t feel right. It’s embarrassing when someone’s already waiting in the back, and I’m late, but I still feel like I have to go around again.
Is your main fear that you'll actually miss something important during the check, or that something bad will happen because of it?

I think it’s… it starts as the fear that I missed something important. Like even if I know I did the safety check, that thought just keeps hitting me, like, what if I missed something on the cab?

But then it turns right into the bad thing part — somebody could get hurt, or my boss could say I lied about checking it. That’s the part that won’t shut up. I’ll be driving, or later I’m trying to study, and it’s still there in my head.

Sorry, I’m kind of circling around it. I guess it’s both, but the missing-something thought is what sets it off.
Is your need to repeat these checks mostly because you want to make sure everything is perfect or because you're afraid of what might happen if something is missed?

It’s more because I’m scared of what happens if I miss something, I think. Like, before I can take a ride, I’ll keep going around the cab checking the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, the paperwork… and then I’ll do the whole thing again.

Sometimes I take pictures, which sounds like it should help, but then I end up staring at the picture like, “Did I actually check it right?” and I start over anyway if it doesn’t feel right. And then the passenger’s sitting there waiting, and I’m already late, and I’m thinking they probably think I’m weird or wasting time—but I still can’t just leave it.
